newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram details rupee rate movements.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram details rupee rate movements.

text.p: The Indian rupee depreciated on average by 0.41 percent a month against the U.S. dollar between April 1996 and January 1997, India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has said.

In a written reply, released on Friday, to a question in the lower house of parliament, Chidambaram said the rupee depreciated on average by 1.22 percent against the British pound during the same period.

The Indian currency appreciated against the Japanese yen, the German mark and the French franc by about 0.66 percent, 0.37 percent and 0.26 percent a month, respectively, during the same period, he said.
Chidambaram said the exchange rate of the rupee is determined by the market.

"The foreign exchange market is monitored closely by the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) and steps are taken, as and when necessary, to counter speculative pressures against the rupee and to maintain orderly foreign exchange market conditions," he said.
"The foreign exchange market has behaved in an orderly fashion in 1996/97 so far," he said, referring to the fiscal year ending on March 31.
At 3:20 p.m. (0950 GMT) on Friday, the rupee was quoted at 35.890/900 against the U.S. dollar.
